ui.ber.below: below the measurement limit, an upper bound
ui.ber.bn.title: noise bandwidth relative to the symbol rate: Bn = 1.12·1.25·Rs = 1.4·Rs
ui.ber.legend: ● CBER from the protocol ({n}) · ○ VBER/LBER · dashed — "<", upper bound · small — threshold run
ui.ber.note: Curves are the ideal model before the decoder (AWGN, Gray coding): QPSK Pb = ½·erfc√(Eb/N0), 8PSK Pb ≈ ⅓·erfc(√(3·Eb/N0)·sin π/8); Eb/N0 = C/N + 10·lg(Bn/(k·Rs)), k = 2 (QPSK) or 3 (8PSK). CBER (before the decoder, ●) is compared with the curve. VBER/LBER (○) are after the decoder — do not compare them with the curve directly. Dashes — the ETSI QEF threshold of the current tuning (no margin).
ui.ber.title: BER(C/N): theory and readings
ui.ch.f.lock.title: from the scan results: the meter showed "MPEG-2 TS"
ui.ch.f.uk.title: narrow U.K. spot beams (28.2°E) are usually not receivable in Ukraine
ui.ch.note: The C/N threshold is the theoretical one for the modulation and FEC (ETSI EN 302 307 / EN 300 421) + 1 dB margin. "Excellent" — margin ≥ 3 dB, "marginal" — 0…3 dB. Databases: KingOfSat, the build date is shown next to the satellite.

ui.geo.decl.title: magnetic declination, east is plus; when set, the compass azimuth is shown
ui.geo.note: Spherical Earth, R = 6371 km, a = 42164 km — a guide for coarse aiming, the maximum is found with the meter; this is not a measurement. Az is from true north, clockwise; a compass shows magnetic (Az magn. = Az − declination). LNB skew: "−" — the satellite is west, "+" — east; fine-tune by maximum MER. Delay is one way.

ui.pair.note: Every 8PSK gets the nearest QPSK of the same position (same polarisation and band, close frequency, ideally the same SR and FEC). Measure pair tunes the meter to both in turn and waits for lock. Yellow — what else differs besides the modulation: a BER difference cannot be put down to the modulation alone.
